fails: The orange impact burst sits at the Moon's bottom edge and spills below and outside the disc. It looks like a floating plus/explosion glyph, not a probe striking the south pole. It also overlaps the Moon's rim awkwardly, and the lower pixel clusters read as a space-invader sprite.

Symmetry break is unclear. The orbiter and rocket are roughly symmetric, and the burst is symmetric too. The one deliberate break (the probe's trajectory or the impact) is not clearly the only asymmetry, because the dotted path, rocket, and star scatter all add asymmetry. This reads as two or more breaks.

Orange is meant to be the protagonist-only token. It is split across the thruster block, the dotted trail and the large burst, so the single protagonist is not obvious and the burst competes with the orbiter.

The Moon is a huge, nearly featureless pale-blue disc. The crater blobs are arbitrary ovals with little variation, which makes the Moon feel flat and dominant. No south-pole or water cue relates it to the article.
The rocket at the far left is cramped against the bottom-left edge. Its base touches the ground bar and its scale is small next to the Moon, so it adds clutter without much meaning.
At thumbnail size the title text turns into a blurry cream smear. The subtitle is unreadable and the orbiter's detail is lost. Only the Moon disc and the orange burst hold as silhouettes.
critic.next_change: Move the orange impact burst up so it sits inside the Moon disc near its lower (south-pole) edge, and shrink it to one compact symmetric cluster with no pieces spilling past the rim. Then drop the subtitle, or enlarge the main title to fill the banner, so the headline survives at 120px.
